# zlanhb

> Returns the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or largest absolute value of a complex Hermitian band matrix using column-major order.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlanhb from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlanhb';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlanhb( order, norm, uplo, N, K, AB, LDAB, WORK ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | Norm type |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part is stored |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super-diagonals or sub-diagonals |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(K + 1) × N</sub> | Band matrix |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANHB as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the band matrix A is supplied.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANHB is set to zero.
- `K`: The number of super-diagonals or sub-diagonals of the band matrix A. $K \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangle of the hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first K+1 rows of `AB`. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(k+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-k) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+k)$. Note that the imaginary parts of the diagonal elements need not be set and are assumed to be zero.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, K + 1 )` (column-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlanhb.ndarray(
    norm, uplo,
    N, K,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

Returns the norm of a complex Hermitian band matrix.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | Norm type: `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part is stored: `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super-diagonals (upper) or sub-diagonals (lower) |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(K + 1) × N</sub> | Band matrix in band storage |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace array (length >= N for `'one-norm'` or `'inf-norm'`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANHB as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the band matrix A is supplied.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANHB is set to zero.
- `K`: The number of super-diagonals or sub-diagonals of the band matrix A. $K \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangle of the hermitian band matrix A, stored in the first K+1 rows of `AB`. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(k+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-k) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+k)$. Note that the imaginary parts of the diagonal elements need not be set and are assumed to be zero.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: result

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import zlanhb from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlanhb';

// Upper Hermitian 4x4 band matrix with K=1 (bandwidth 1):

// Full Hermitian matrix:

//   [ 2        (-3+1i)   0        0       ]

//   [ (-3-1i)   4        (1+2i)   0       ]

//   [ 0        (1-2i)   -5        (6-3i)  ]

//   [ 0         0       (6+3i)    7       ]

// Band storage (column-major, LDAB=2):

//   [ *          (-3+1i)    (1+2i)     (6-3i) ]  <- superdiag

//   [ (2,0)      (4,0)      (-5,0)     (7,0)  ]  <- diagonal
const AB = new Complex128Array( [ 0, 0, 2, 0, -3, 1, 4, 0, 1, 2, -5, 0, 6, -3, 7, 0 ] );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 4 );

console.log( 'Max norm:', zlanhb.ndarray( 'max', 'upper', 4, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, WORK, 1, 0 ) );
console.log( 'One norm:', zlanhb.ndarray( 'one-norm', 'upper', 4, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, WORK, 1, 0 ) );
console.log( 'Inf norm:', zlanhb.ndarray( 'inf-norm', 'upper', 4, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, WORK, 1, 0 ) );
console.log( 'Frobenius norm:', zlanhb.ndarray( 'frobenius', 'upper', 4, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, WORK, 1, 0 ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLANHB`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLANHB returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of an n by n hermitian band matrix A, with k super-diagonals.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{ZLANHB} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(A(i,j))) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
